summary: The preregistered BTC-displacement to SOL/XRP relative-overextension residual-reclaim payoff was hard-valid but strongly negative. The parent opportunity screen supplied 163 unique decision events on four previously unopened December 2023 dates. All four structural confirmation/stop variants failed at both 100 ms and 300 ms. The least-negative frozen-order candidate C50_S10 made 129 trades; at 18 bp its 100 ms path averaged -19.0024 bp per trade, median -14.6261 bp, PF 0.01550, total -2451.31 bp, exact top-10%-winner-removed total -2456.60 bp, and zero of four positive dates. The 300 ms path averaged -19.1346 bp, median -14.4753 bp, PF 0.01472, total -2468.37 bp and zero positive dates. The exact payoff is retired without adjacent threshold tuning. The opportunity state appears to describe continuation or irregular exhaustion rather than a repeatable residual-reclaim reversal.
trader_translation: BTC displacement followed by a high-attention SOL/XRP extension beyond beta-implied equilibrium was treated as a relative external-liquidity raid. Entry required BTC non-confirmation and a completed 25% or 50% residual reclaim, then traded opposite the follower extension with a stop beyond the post-raid extreme and a target at relative equilibrium. That sequence did not produce positive expectancy.

interpretation.supported: The overreaction state exists with adequate event density across the four pre-2024 sample dates.
interpretation.rejected: A completed partial residual reclaim after the state does not identify a profitable mean-reversion entry at realistic cost and latency.
interpretation.retired_dependency: BTC-to-alt high-attention relative overextension followed by 25%/50% residual-reclaim reversal using the frozen parent event formula.
interpretation.next_information_requirement: Change the information source or payoff mechanism; do not tune adjacent reclaim or stop thresholds. A materially different continuation payoff may only be tested under a new preregistration and untouched dates.
